I used to play it for PS4. I'm really conflicted on Destiny. Gameplay-wise, it had the best shooter mechanics I've ever played on a console. Headshotting enemies was incredibly satisfying, and the different ability and builds were fun to play around with.

The very first raid, the Vault of Glass, was easily the best piece of content in the game. The issue? You need a 6 person team to play it, and there is no automatic matchmaking. Okay, well you can always make friends in the game, right? Well, not easily. Before I quit playing, they did allow mic communication in strikes, but you had to opt in. Combine that with the fact that the feature took so long to come out, almost nobody talked in strikes. I mean at that point, everyone could pretty much run the strikes in their sleep so there wasn't anything to talk about.

Fortunately the community stepped in and developed tools for matchmaking. The problem now? Getting together a competent team of 6. It wasn't impossible but you would run in to some real jackasses doing this, like in any game I suppose. I tried like hell to get into a 'normal' team so I could stop doing pick up groups, but as soon as I would establish something, the group would stop getting online.

So the social aspect of the game is entirely lacking, yet is required to tackle the very best content in the game. Also there's a HUGE grind to level your weapons and armor. Once you hit level 20, your level starts relying on the Light stat of your gear. You can increase the light stat some by leveling the weapon and unlocking upgrades. So now if you're playing and find a new badass piece of gear, you can't wear it because your Light will decrease and you'll lose levels. So you have to grind exp for it before you can even wear it. Depending on the equipment, it could be a few days or a week before you can actually wear it.

AND THEN, the 1st expansion The Dark Below came out. It added a few cool things like new weapons and armor, new strikes and story levels. And it added a new raid. This new raid didn't come close to the Vault of Glass. Rather than being hard by virtue of the mechanics of the dungeon, they simply throw higher level enemies at you, while leaving entire areas of the raid completely skippable by way of glitches.

What's the problem with throwing higher level enemies at you? Well, the raids have normal and hard modes. The hard mode raids are the end all be all of Destiny content. It's the most challenging and you get the best rewards. The problem is, the new raid's hard mode locks the enemies 1 level above what you could even attain. But it's just 1 level right? Well the leveling system in Destiny SUCKS. I already mentioned HOW you have to level, and the grind involved. But the way Destiny works, your level is the MOST IMPORTANT STAT in the game.

A 1 level difference between you and your enemies yields a huge penalty. If you're level 30, and your enemy is level 31, you do 33% less damage to them AND take 33% more damage from them automatically. So that's where the difficulty comes from in this new raid. Not from the mechanics like Vault of Glass, but from utilizing their terrible leveling system to hamper your DPS and survivablility.

I stopped playing after the hard mode raid was unlocked for The Dark Below. At this point, I saw what Bungie really cared for. Artificial difficulty and artificial game lengthening through excessive grinding. Content drips out slowly, and the same activities are repeated week on end. There's no good way to make friends in the game.

Man I did not expect to go on that long. So I haven't played the 2nd expansion House of Wolves. I hear it did a lot to improve Destiny for everyone. There are ways to power up your old gear, so the stuff you spent hours grinding for isn't suddenly underpowered, and I think going forward they'll take more care to avoid EXCESSIVE grinding. There will always be some grind, but I think they'll respect the time you put into the game now. I have no idea if the social aspect has improved.

With the next expansion coming out, I see things getting better. If you have friends interested in the game, I'd say it's worth it to try. The Vault of Glass alone is something I would highly recommend experiencing, hopefully with people who won't completely spoil it. I imagine playing this on PC would be incredibly fun, but I'll wait and see how interested my friends are.

I had a quick look but couldn't see a thread for this yet, so have just gone through the dev posts in the announcement thread on the Frontier forums (https://forums.frontier.co.uk/showthread.php?t=172167)) to pick out what info they have confirmed so far:

  • Anyone with a lifetime expansion pass gets Horizons (and the Cobra MkIV) free on release.
  • Some development will apply to all versions of the game and so will be available to all owners. This will typically apply to features that apply to everyone in game. Other features and content will be for Elite Dangerous: Horizons owners only.
  • The price is for a full season of expansions, not just planetary landing.
  • No walking around in this season - that's coming much later in a future season.
  • If you already have Premium Beta access or higher then you will have beta access. Otherwise you need to pre-order it with beta access.
  • It's PC only for now. Other platforms are further down the line.
  • Not revealing dates for beta yet.
  • People with and without Horizons will still be able to play together, but any content specific to Elite Dangerous: Horizons won't be available. So if you fly onto a planet surface then they won't be able to follow.
  • Pre-orders only available through their store. Will only be able to purchase Horizons directly through Steam after release.
  • Anyone who already owns Elite: Dangerous and buys Horizons will get access to the Cobra MkIV
  • Planets with life and atmospheres are further down the line, not within the season (so are not included in the Horizons price). "We've always said that we'd come at it in stages - it's a massive amount of development!"
  • Looting and crafting system is due early 2016, so is included in Horizons season/price
